Exact gradients for the sampled objective are feasible without materializing B×L×128×D embeddings. Proposed implementation: compute encoder features once; create a detached, gradient-enabled feature proxy; process valid positions in chunks, each retaining all 129 candidates. Backpropagate each chunk’s summed cross-entropy divided by the total valid-position count, accumulating item-embedding and proxy gradients; finally backpropagate the proxy gradient through the encoder. Step once after accumulation, preserving both gradient paths for tied embeddings. Merely summing chunk losses before backward retains their graphs. Alternatively, checkpoint embedding lookup and scoring with `use_reentrant=False`, retaining sampled IDs for identical recomputation. These follow [PyTorch autograd](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/autograd.html) and [checkpointing](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/checkpoint) semantics. Exact means the same sampled objective, up to floating-point differences; separate softmaxes over negative chunks change it. Verify against a tiny unchunked reference.

Recommended ablations: preregister a small baseline-plus-one-change matrix, equal aggregate GPU-second caps, fixed seeds 0/42, identical validation cadence, and a checkpoint rule. Charge debugging, diagnostics, and failed runs to 43,200 GPU-seconds; four slots change concurrency, not budget. Reserve a fixed confirmation allocation before exploration. Limit adaptive variants and checkpoint comparisons; retain the baseline for inconclusive gains. Repeated validation selection can overfit substantially ([Cawley–Talbot](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)); reusing validation for confirmation does not make it independent.

Store paired per-user hit indicators. Bootstrap user indices jointly across models within each dataset; calculate each dataset’s mean difference, then average four differences for a 95% interval ([paired bootstrap](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). One hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points, macro HR by 0.125. Intervals condition on seeds and fixed candidates, exclude training variability, and do not correct selection bias. Report the unchanged sampled benchmark: it need not preserve full-catalog rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).
